# Introduction

SpatialData is a versatile data framework for processing spatial omics data in python. This tutorial demonstrates how to convert a SpatialData object saved on disk to a Giotto object with `GiottoConnect::spatialdataToGiotto()`.

Exporting a Giotto object to SpatialData (`giottoToSpatialData()`) was retired in GiottoClass 0.8.0; export will be revisited in GiottoConnect.

# Set up

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Ensure Giotto Suite and GiottoConnect are installed.
if(!"Giotto" %in% installed.packages()) {
  pak::pkg_install("giotto-suite/Giotto")
}
if(!"GiottoConnect" %in% installed.packages()) {
  pak::pkg_install("giotto-suite/GiottoConnect")
}

library(Giotto)
library(GiottoConnect)
```

`spatialdataToGiotto()` runs Python in your R session, unlike the Python tools
described in [Python in Giotto Suite](python.html). Give it a Python
installation that has the `spatialdata` and `scanpy` modules installed:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
python_path <- "/path/to/python" # with spatialdata and scanpy installed
```

# Save the SpatialData object

In Python, save your SpatialData object on disk:

```{python, eval = FALSE}
# Let's say your spatialdata object is called sdata:
sdata.write("save_folder")
```

This creates a folder "save_folder" with subfolders 'images', 'shapes', and 'tables' for each component of the SpatialData object.

# spatialdataToGiotto()

If you had nearest neighbor or spatial networks created or stored within your SpatialData, you can also include them in the conversion by either providing a .txt file or a list of the names of the keys for these networks.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
converted_gobject <- spatialdataToGiotto(
    spatialdata_path = "save_folder",
    n_key_added = "cell_rna_nn_network_keys_added.txt",
    spatial_n_key_added = "cell_rna_spatial_network_keys_added.txt",
    python_path = python_path
)
```

# Session Info

```{r, eval = FALSE}
sessionInfo()
```
